FINDING_ID: IM_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.97  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.83  
DESCRIPTION: In [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5872), `apply_diagnosis()` creates `_remediation_state` even when P-pass rejects the fix and `_apply_transform()` never runs. `_verify_remediation_outcomes()` then logs success/failure for a remediation that never happened and advances the chain anyway.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Only create remediation state after a real adjustment is applied. For P-pass rejects/skips, record a separate rejected/deferred outcome and do not feed `_verify_remediation_outcomes()`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.92  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74  
DESCRIPTION: In [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5150), `process_round()` calls `record_model_round()` without `response_time` or `response_chars`, so they stay at `0`. That makes `parser_yield` and `cpf_spike` detection paths unreachable through the manager integration even though they work when called directly.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Pass `response_time=resp.response_time` and `response_chars=len(resp.content)` when a response exists, and pass explicit zeros only for true no-response cases.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.90  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.77  
DESCRIPTION: In [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5153), immune per-model failure tracking uses `failed = mid not in responses or not responses[mid].parseable` and iterates over `self.models`. That misses real `EMPTY`, `TIMEOUT`, `FORMAT`, and `UNDERPERFORM` failures already detected by `FailureHandler`, and it also keeps counting already-benched models as failing forever.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Derive `failed` from the actual `failure_type` or recovery action, and track active models separately from excluded ones so benched models do not keep poisoning consecutive-failure logic.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.88  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69  
DESCRIPTION: In [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2781), `DetectorHealthMonitor.record_round()` hard-codes `0.04` for vocab saturation detection instead of using the live `tau_vocab_growth`. After remediation lowers `self.config.tau_vocab_growth`, the health monitor still diagnoses against the stale threshold.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Give the health monitor access to the current config, or pass the active vocab threshold into `record_round()` so diagnosis and remediation use the same parameter value.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.86  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72  
DESCRIPTION: In [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5583), the `vocab_saturation` chain changes the threshold, but outcome verification in [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3076) judges success by whether raw `vocab_growth` increased. A threshold tweak can fix the decision boundary without making the underlying metric rise, so successful recalibration is misclassified as failure.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Verify threshold-changing remediations against the detector decision they are meant to correct, such as “pathology no longer fires” or “stop predicate no longer trips prematurely,” not against the raw metric itself.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.82  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.68  
DESCRIPTION: In [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5698), damping is enforced by `diagnosis.detector`, but the config comment says it should be “minimum rounds between adjustments to the same parameter.” This blocks unrelated fixes from the same detector and fails to protect the same parameter if a different detector mutates it.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Key damping on the actual adjustment target, such as `(parameter, scope)` where scope is global or model-specific, and keep `detector` as audit metadata only.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.79  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61  
DESCRIPTION: In [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5639), `add_synthesis_directive` only writes to models that have no existing `per_model_directives` entry. The same pattern appears in the verification-miscalibration fix at [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5738). If Phase A already loaded directives from the registry, these immune remediations silently do nothing.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Append or merge immune directives into existing per-model directives, with truncation at `max_per_model_directive_chars`, instead of treating any existing directive as immutable.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F008  
SEVERITY: 0.78  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.47  
DESCRIPTION: In [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4347), `FailureHandler.get_recovery()` checks `same_type_count >= n_fail` before recording the current failure. With `n_fail=2`, escalation happens on the third same failure, not the second; mechanically, the PM timeout path yields `RETRY`, `RETRY`, `ABORT`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Include the current failure in the threshold check, for example `same_type_count + 1 >= n_fail`, or record first and then compute escalation from updated history.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
